# Finite responsiveness to aggregation within same-kind recoverable basic losses

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`finite-aggregation-within-restorable-basic-losses` · **reviewed-scoped** · argument · F07 · [record](finite-aggregation-within-restorable-basic-losses.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> FR proposes: among independently specified same-kind recoverable basic losses, where support, burdens and history persist with scale, a finite scale of joint lesser protection should acquire sufficient grounds for choice over a fixed graver loss; strict loss matching laws give its formal content.

<a id="exact-statement--确切陈述"></a>
## Exact statement

Strict loss matching obeys the laws below on every frame (Becoming.LossMatching). On these laws FR proposes that, within an independently specified family of same-kind recoverable basic losses, a fixed graver loss should not retain sufficient priority over arbitrarily many fixed lesser basic protections solely through its gravity difference. Where support, burdens and historical conditions persist under scale expansion, some finite scale of joint protection should acquire sufficient grounds for choice. This is an additional normative candidate beyond LR’s neighborhood, with affirmative defense and author counterreview, not a consequence of existing axioms; the laws state its exact formal content, not its warrant. One repair process is an instance (laws 7–9).

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. A generative extension is a strict loss match by identity, so a commitment making strict matching sufficient for strict priority contains comparison principle C, and not conversely: in the repair instance the match of A against B₁ is no extension. (`Becoming.Frame.StrictLossMatch`, `Becoming.Frame.strictLossMatch_of_extension`, `Becoming.Frame.SufficientMatching`, `Becoming.Frame.SufficientMatching.comparison`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.a_b1_not_extension`, `Becoming.MatchedCourses.a_b1_not_extension`)
2. The commitment is consistent only where matching is asymmetric; with infinitely many losses a configuration can strictly match itself, so finiteness is needed. (`Becoming.Frame.SufficientMatching.not_mutual`, `Becoming.EndlessLosses.self_match`, `Becoming.EndlessLosses.no_sufficient_matching`)
3. With losses listed once, strict matching is irreflexive and asymmetric: the worse configuration loses strictly more. (`Becoming.Frame.StrictLossMatch.length_lt`)
4. The counting law: with content read as a class and losses listed once, a strict match exists exactly when the better configuration loses no more in each class and fewer in all; within one class, exactly when it loses fewer. (`Becoming.Frame.strictLossMatch_iff_counts`, `Becoming.Frame.strictLossMatch_iff_length_of_alike`)
5. Where every claim rests on a common support and claims are finitely listed, a configuration that loses that support is strictly better by matching than no configuration, under any content relation. (`Becoming.Frame.not_strictLossMatch_of_base_lost`)
6. By definition, a frame that reads a claim at its episode time keeps a missed claim missed when support returns, and it reads the claim at that time exactly when the claim's realization is settled from then on; where a claim is missed and later realized again, no support makes the frame read it at the earlier time. Whether an actual frame reads at episode time is the premise. (`Becoming.Frame.readsAt_iff_settled`, `Becoming.Frame.ReadsAt.loss_retained`, `Becoming.Frame.not_readsAt_of_recovery`)
7. Instance: the courses of one repair process are generated from one start and retain two episodes at the same position against one, two or three elsewhere; read as one class of complete episodes, the four courses retain 3, 4, 3 and 2 losses, so by the counting law A strictly matches B₁, B₃ strictly matches A, and B₂ and A match neither way. (`Becoming.RepairComparison.common_start`, `Becoming.MatchedCourses.common_start`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.generated_trace`, `Becoming.MatchedCourses.generated_trace`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.separated_same_life`, `Becoming.MatchedCourses.separated_same_position`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.matches_iff`, `Becoming.MatchedCourses.matches_iff`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.lost_counts`, `Becoming.MatchedCourses.lost_counts`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.a_matches_b1`, `Becoming.MatchedCourses.a_matches_b1`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.b3_matches_a`, `Becoming.MatchedCourses.b3_matches_a`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.a_matches_b1_by_count`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.b3_matches_a_by_count`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.b2_a_neither`, `Becoming.MatchedCourses.b2_a_neither`)
8. Under sufficient complete-episode matching one protection is insufficient and three suffice, while two against two supplies only a loss correspondence. (`Becoming.RepairComparison.SufficientMatching`, `Becoming.Frame.SufficientMatching`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.sufficientMatching_iff`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.conditional_lower_anchor`, `Becoming.MatchedCourses.conditional_lower_anchor`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.conditional_upper_anchor`, `Becoming.MatchedCourses.conditional_upper_anchor`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.b2_loss_correspondence`, `Becoming.MatchedCourses.b2_loss_correspondence`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.b2_correspondence_involutive`, `Becoming.MatchedCourses.b2_correspondence_involutive`)
9. Where the three-access repair disconnects the common backbone, that course is strictly better by matching than no course. (`Becoming.RepairComparison.fragile_b3_loses_backbone`, `Becoming.MatchedCourses.fragile_b3_loses_base`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.fragile_b3_not_matching`, `Becoming.MatchedCourses.fragile_b3_not_matching`, `Becoming.RepairComparison.fragile_b3_better_than_none`, `Becoming.MatchedCourses.fragile_b3_matches_nothing`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- Reuses G0’s interface in the current significance structure and J’s practical scope; FR is an additional revisable comparison commitment, not a new Part I theorem or second fundamental axiom.
- H and fixed L are complete actual basic losses of an independently described common kind; recovery is reachable and timely, intervening support is real, and terminal harm, unrepeatable participation, common collapse, different coercion and undertakings are not omitted.
- Distinct living realizations, reliable jointly feasible protection and independent permission are established; scale-dependent burdens and live chance commitments enter comparison. FR does not guarantee physical scalability.
- That joint lesser basic protection can become sufficient for choice is FR’s explicit normative commitment; it is not derived from finite duration, physical continuity or causal dependence. Rejecting permanent gravity priority still permits incomparability or chances on both sides, and is therefore not equivalent to FR’s sufficiency commitment.
- The repair instance supplies a repair law, backbone and coverage capacities. Support sufficiency for the activity, complete equivalent episodes and absence of omitted cumulative consequences require independent correspondence. Current support restoration is not complete experiential or relational recovery.
- SufficientMatching explicitly adds sufficient choice force for a distinct strict loss match preserving complete content within independently established scope. It strengthens LC and extends BC1 sufficiency to these complete activity episodes. Only composition of the outer comparisons additionally requires Transitive Le.
- In the account of decomposition and sustained harm, completeness concerns the actual comparison and evidenced decision-relevant relations. Joint effects may be represented separately without disappearing, and identical background retains its role. Potentially decisive unknown effects require inquiry or warranted bounds.
- Whole-course references must first have independently sufficient warrant, then feed actual improvement/worsening into the same warranted comparison and scoped transitivity. BC2/LC pro tanto reasons cannot replace sufficient anchors, and an isolated gravity change does not establish preservation of whole response outcomes.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- The repair instance treats only the constructed domain where the graver side independently decomposes into two complete equivalent activity losses; it does not calibrate the arbitrary H of FR’s general form.
- No universal exchange rate, global ranking, minimum sufficient number (in the instance or for arbitrary H) or final two-against-two verdict follows.
- Neither general FR nor formal consistency with all earlier principles is shown.
- This case cannot dismiss CP claims or valid chances outside its warranted scope.
- The account of decomposition gives no unique natural partition for every harm and no actual certification of all aftereffects.
- Either whole reference may be unavailable; needing an upper bound does not warrant one.
- The counting law is an exact criterion only where content is read as a class and losses are listed once; for other content only the necessary direction is proved.
- **Counterexample:** A saturating rival can count every lesser loss while imposing a permanent ceiling; a chance rival requires a positive chance for the graver claimant at every scale. Neither is logically excluded; they identify substantive disagreement and what FR forgoes. [source](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/CROSSED-CLAIMS-ARGUMENT.md)
- **Counterexample:** Equal recovery endpoints can conceal unrepeatable losses; scale can undermine support or increase imposed burdens, defeating application. Finitude does not entail ethical exchangeability. [source](../../chapters/BASIC-CONFLICT-JUDGMENT.md)
- **Counterexample:** When the supplied equipment law makes the three-access installation disconnect the backbone, protection fails and the common loss remains; fragile_b3_not_matching excludes the original matching. The general law: where every claim rests on the backbone, a course losing it is strictly better by matching than no course (not_strictLossMatch_of_base_lost; here fragile_b3_better_than_none, under any content reading). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/history/becoming/Becoming/RepairComparison.lean)
- **Counterexample:** Continuous nondecomposable damage, cumulative depletion or unrestored trust can defeat episode correspondence. Even with equivalent consequences, concentration may normatively challenge sufficiency and cannot invariably be classified as missing facts. [source](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/CROSSED-CLAIMS-ARGUMENT.md)
- **Counterexample:** Two disconnections within one sustained task do not automatically become two whole losses; equal endpoints and brief restoration do not erase aftereffects. Filling the repair instance’s recovery gap can supply worsening for its insufficient anchor, but cannot automatically preserve three-protection sufficiency. [source](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/CROSSED-CLAIMS-ARGUMENT.md)
- **Counterexample:** EndlessLosses: with infinitely many losses a configuration strictly matches itself (EndlessLosses.self_match), and the sufficiency commitment is inconsistent there (EndlessLosses.no_sufficient_matching), so finitely many complete episodes are needed. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/LossMatching.lean)

**Standard boundaries:** Premise-free (zero-substantive-axiom) grounding is a separate open target; completed results on the conditional alignment route keep their scope.

<details><summary>Correspondence, dependencies, sources and history</summary>

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Identify living positions and complete gains/losses through formation, failure and repair of one support activity; do not shrink L into trivial conveniences with population, duplicate a life or dependency path, or define sameness/basicness by the ranking. Actual sufficiency thresholds require further comparative warrant. The repair instance first generates the courses through one Process/Run; historical_claim_iff_support checks the record against actual support at its episode time, retaining identity, time and the backbone. sameEpisode encodes a proposed reading without certifying real equivalence; scope cannot be defined by a desired winner. The account of decomposition and sustained harm distinguishes temporal narration, differentiated actual losses and comparative substitutability. Restoration is neither necessary for every decomposition nor sufficient for equal counting. Sustained harm retains present experience, activity/self-care, restoration paths/burdens, common support and further generation without treating these aspects as additive scores.
